clue.text: Virginia, retiring girl, is a humble dependant

parts.note: VA is the standard abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for a girl is read from right to left

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A shy young woman from Virginia is described as a lowly hanger-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns the girl round. It looks like a description of a shy girl, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times a vassal held land from a lord in return for service, a subordinate position.

clue.text: Watch the head angle

parts.note: to view is to watch
a head, or headland, is a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch the tilt of the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' reads as part of the body but is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle on something is a particular perspective or way of seeing it.

clue.text: It is important for Stock Exchange heads to have the right credit notes

indicators.note: heads asks for the leading letter of each of the two words

parts.note: R is short for right
IOUs are written promises to pay, notes acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: Stock Exchange chiefs must hold the right financial paper.
explanation.walkthrough: IOUs are 'I owe you' notes, credit given on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weighty or significant, not to be taken lightly, is both.

clue.text: Their suggestions are always constructive

parts.note: constructive is read literally: these professionals' proposals are for buildings to be constructed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Constructive' usually means helpful criticism; here it means leading to construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Building designers propose plans that are meant to be built.

clue.text: A graduate register may be reduced

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a table is a list or register of figures or names

explanation.surface: A student who has graduated sees their name on a list that could be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen, so something that can be lessened in amount or force qualifies.

clue.text: Appealing for reform, see about involving University

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the university letter goes inside
reform means form anew, so the letters of see and about are reshaped

explanation.surface: A campaigner calls for change at a university, petitioning about its affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges the eight letters into BEAUTEOS, and 'involving' takes the University letter inside. 'Appealing' looks like pleading, but it means attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauteous is a poetic word for beautiful, and so attractive.

clue.text: Sort the letters

definitions.meaning: a sort is a kind or variety
in printing, the letters are the characters set for a page

explanation.definitionFit: Type means both a kind or category, and the printed characters on a page.

clue.text: Talk big about the family causing a slowing down

indicators.note: about means going around, so the boasting word surrounds the family word

parts.note: to brag is to talk big, or boast
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A family boaster brings everything to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the boast round the family. Talking big is boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying the brakes reduces a vehicle's speed, so it is a deceleration.

clue.text: Stand taken by the painter

parts.note: a stand here is a supporting frame, the one an artist props a canvas on, not a position taken in an argument

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand taken' suggests an opinion or position the painter adopts, but it is a physical frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's wooden frame holding a canvas upright while working.

clue.text: Some men like pictures for capital investment

indicators.note: some means part of the following words, so the letters run across them

explanation.surface: Some men like paintings as a way to invest money.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across liKE PIctures. 'capital investment' suggests finance, but it is what you invest your head (capital) with.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French military cap, worn on the head, so a cap put on.

clue.text: A race he organised caused complaint

indicators.note: organised means arranged into a new order, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone set up a running event and it drew grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges A RACE HE. 'Complaint' reads as a grumble but means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint can mean an illness or ailment, and a pain in the ear is one such.

clue.text: Looks for a variety of fruit in addition

indicators.note: in tells us the fruit sits within the letters for the addition

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an addition at the end of a letter
a pear is one kind of fruit

explanation.surface: Someone searches for an extra kind of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the fruit inside the postscript. 'Looks for' reads as searching, but 'Looks' alone means 'seems'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean seems: 'he looks tired' and 'he appears tired' say the same thing.

clue.text: "Soften and support it?", one scoffed

parts.note: to prop is to support
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
scoffed in the sense of ate greedily

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to cushion and back a proposal, and is mocked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' looks like mockery but is the slang for eating greedily, giving ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease or placate someone is to soften their anger.

clue.text: Fell down

definitions.meaning: a fell is a ... or moor in northern England
a down is a rolling chalk upland, as in the South Downs of southern England

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like verbs of falling, but each is a noun for upland country in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Fells and downs are both stretches of raised ground, in the north and south of England respectively.

clue.text: Still state this is not the country for women

definitions.meaning: a condition of not moving or not flowing

definitions.text: this is not the country for women
definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading of a nation open only to men

explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is inactivity, while a stag party is men only, so a stag nation would exclude women.

clue.text: Substituting for sainted characters

indicators.note: characters means the letters themselves, which are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for the holy ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' asks for the letters of SAINTED in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as 'instead of', it means in place of or as a replacement for something.

clue.text: The newspapers indeed make one despondent!

annotationWithheld.why: The newspapers indeed make one despondent!: the only parse reads 'indeed' as IN DEED, so the one word 'indeed' is both the container indicator 'in' and the leaf DEED, which the check refuses as a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: The newspapers indeed make one despondent!

clue.text: Figure the senior officer is wearing a tab

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
a tag is a tab or label
having something on means wearing it, so on follows the item worn

explanation.surface: A commanding officer has a label pinned to his uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: An officer with a tag on: the word for wearing comes after the thing worn, as in 'with a coat on'. OC, Officer Commanding, is a British army title.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided shape is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Drinks enabling people to sleep tight?

definitions.text: Drinks enabling people to sleep tight

parts.words: Drinks enabling people to sleep tight
parts.note: a bedtime drink of spirits helps one sleep, and tight also hints at being drunk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep tight' is a bedtime wish, but tight also means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholic drinks taken just before bed are named for the caps once worn in bed.

clue.text: Pas de deux?

parts.note: the ballet term translated word for word from French is 'step of two', read back into English as a dance name

explanation.walkthrough: A pas de deux is a ballet duet, but taken literally pas is step and deux is two, giving a ballroom dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the French phrase means a step for two, matching the name of a quick ballroom dance.

clue.text: Moving to time, many skipped

indicators.note: moving means shifting the letters of to time into a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, many

explanation.surface: Moving with the time meant many steps were missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges the six letters into OMITTE. Roman numerals for big numbers often stand for 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left out or passed over has been skipped.

clue.text: "Welcome ever smiles, and farewell goes out _" (Troi. and Cres.)

definitions.text: Welcome ever smiles, and farewell goes out _" (Troi. and Cres

parts.words: Welcome ever smiles, and farewell goes out _" (Troi. and Cres
parts.note: a line from Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida with its last word blanked out for the solver to supply

explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses tells Achilles that welcome always smiles while farewell leaves with a sad breath.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes Shakespeare's line, describing a farewell leaving with sorrowful breaths.

clue.text: Repeat it over a long period, note

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a long period of history
te is the seventh note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone is told to say it again and again over an age, by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To say or do something again is a repetition.

clue.text: Steal, so confine to bed

definitions.meaning: to copy or pilfer someone else's work
a ... is a child's bed, so to ... is to shut in such a bed

explanation.definitionFit: Crib means both to plagiarise and, as a noun or verb, a cot for an infant.

clue.text: The holder is about to set the price

parts.note: C, from circa, means about
to rate is to set a value or price on something

explanation.surface: The owner of the company is about to fix the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holder' suggests an owner, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a box or case that holds goods.

clue.text: Writing about member perhaps meant preparing to do battle again

parts.note: Re, as at the head of a business letter, is used when writing about a subject
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word meant might be in some other order

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on an MP may have meant the country was getting ready for war again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MEANT into AMENT. 'member' suggests a Member of Parliament but means a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearming is supplying fresh weapons, which a nation does when readying itself for renewed fighting.

clue.text: Sudden attack from the tall grass

definitions.meaning: a charge or onslaught made all at once
tall marsh plants with stems used for mats

explanation.definitionFit: A rush is both a charge at speed and a marsh plant with long stems.

clue.text: River responsible for erosion

definitions.meaning: the ... flows through Durham in north-east England
gradual damage by rubbing or use

explanation.definitionFit: The Wear is a river in Durham; wear also means the gradual wearing away of surfaces.

clue.text: Player inserting key in a lock

indicators.note: inserting tells us the musical key is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone puts a key into a door lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inserting' puts C between A and TRESS. 'Lock' and 'key' suggest a door; here they are hair and music.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a stage or screen performer, one who plays a part.

clue.text: A bloomer puts a rascal back in deep water

indicators.note: in places the turned-round letters within the word for deep water

parts.note: the sea is deep water

indicators.note: back means the phrase a rascal is read from right to left

parts.note: a rip is a rascal or rogue

explanation.surface: Someone shoves a scoundrel back into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the phrase into PIRA, which 'in' puts inside the deep water. 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or loaf; it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiraea is a flowering shrub, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Lead door specially made for the Treasury

indicators.note: specially made means put together to order, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A lead-lined door is custom built for the government finance department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially made' rearranges LEAD DOOR. 'Treasury' suggests the finance ministry, but here it is a store of treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold, a fabled hoard of riches.

clue.text: If not a French one, then minor

parts.note: un is French for a or one
less means smaller or minor

explanation.surface: If it is not a French one, then it is the lesser one.
explanation.definitionFit: It means except on condition that, a conjunction equivalent to if not.
